cats.name: Basecat
cats.whoIsTheCat: A cream kitten in a blue construction hard hat, hugging a blue 'base' bottle, from a 'Weekend vibes:' meme that Coinbase Wallet (@CoinbaseWallet, ~440K followers) posted on X on 15 Aug 2026. The token launched on o1 Launchpad the same day and the kitten became the helmeted mascot of Base memes. The real kitten in the photo has not been identified.

virality.summary: Coinbase Wallet's 'Weekend vibes:' post (15 Aug 2026) showed the helmeted kitten dreaming of two bottles of blue 'base' juice. The community ran with it: on 16 Aug @BasecatOnBase quoted Coinbase Wallet asking 'Is this real?' ('you posted the cat. the timeline built the army.'), Cobie followed the account, Coinbase's CBO Shan Aggarwal followed, and Coinbase Wallet replied 'Cats crave it.' Coinbase put BASECAT on its listing roadmap on 21 Aug and opened trading on 24 Aug; Gate added futures on 2 Sep; on 3 Sep Base's own 'pick your seat' meme gave the helmeted cat seat 6, next to Cobie.

cats.lore: On a sunny Saturday in August 2026, Coinbase Wallet posted a little 'Weekend vibes' doodle: a cream kitten in a blue hard hat, hugging one bottle of blue juice and dreaming of two. Base builders saw themselves in it. By the next day the timeline was full of helmeted cats, the community had built the kitten a home, and Coinbase Wallet itself was asking 'Is this real?' Base later saved the kitten seat 6 in its 'pick your seat' meme. Today Basecat is run by its community, who hand a blue helmet to anyone ready to make something.

cats.name: Simon's Cat
cats.catName: Simon's Cat (based on Simon Tofield's cat Hugh)
cats.whoIsTheCat: The hungry white cartoon cat of British animator Simon Tofield, based mainly on his own cat Hugh. The first film, 'Cat Man Do', went up on YouTube on 4 March 2008 and won Best Comedy at the 2008 British Animation Awards. The series grew into books, games and a 6.6M-subscriber channel. Simon's Cat Ltd is now a Banijay UK company, which licensed the CAT token in 2024.

virality.summary: Tofield made 'Cat Man Do' to teach himself Flash: a cat trying everything to get Simon out of bed for breakfast. It won Best Comedy at the 2008 British Animation Awards and made the cat's pointing-at-his-mouth 'feed me' gesture world famous. There followed 148 main-series episodes (2008-2026), 10 books from Canongate (from 2009), Disney-made shorts (2012), a Daily Mirror strip (2011-13), a Sesame Street tie-in (2016) and several mobile games. The official channel is one of YouTube's biggest animation channels.
virality.metrics: 'Cat Man Do' (uploaded 4 Mar 2008): 66,995,386 views, 338,098 likes. Channel: 6.59M subscribers, 1,796,640,967 views, 810 videos, joined 14 Nov 2007, United Kingdom. X @SimonsCat: 461,801 followers; token account @SimonsCatMeme: 107,101. All read 2026-09-25 ~20:40 UTC. Token docs claim 25M+ social followers and 2.8M users of the Telegram mini-app. CoinGecko: 119,627 watchlist users. GeckoTerminal: 283,772 BSC holders.

coin.launched: 2024-08-22 on BNB Chain (Banijay press release, token docs); earliest BSC pool 2024-08-21 23:36 UTC per DexScreener. Solana version followed 2024-11-18 (first Solana pools, DexScreener)

coin.endorsedByOwner: Yes, by the IP holder. Banijay Rights announced on 27 Aug 2024 that Simon's Cat (a Banijay UK company) lends its name to the $CAT token, in a deal with Anonymous Labs, with Floki/TokenFi running the presale. The deal included a donation to Cats Protection. The token docs say Banijay Group authorised use of the brand, likeness and assets. No personal statement from Simon Tofield was found.

cats.lore: In 2008 British animator Simon Tofield taught himself Flash with a short film about his cat trying everything to get him out of bed for breakfast. The cat was drawn mostly from his own cat, Hugh. 'Cat Man Do' won Best Comedy at the British Animation Awards, and a hungry white cat pointing at his mouth became a worldwide language. Since then he has chased birds, pestered the garden hedgehog and demanded dinner across books, games and 800-plus videos. In 2024 the brand lent its name to the CAT token, and the launch came with a donation to feed cats at Cats Protection while they waited for homes.

look.signature: The 'feed me' gesture: sits up and jabs a paw at his open mouth (or taps an empty bowl), staring with huge round eyes. The token logo shows the same wide-eyed stare from close up.
look.poseHint: Sit upright facing the viewer. On click, point at the mouth twice with a short 'meow', then look hopeful. Idle: slow blink, ear twitch, tail flick.

cats.name: Thinking Cat
cats.whoIsTheCat: A tabby-and-white cat with one paw curled under the chin, from 'Thinking Cat', a photo Douglas Sacha published on Fine Art America on 5 Feb 2019. It became the 'Cat Thinking' reaction meme on TikTok in January 2025 and spread on TikTok and Instagram that February. The cat's name and home are not documented. $HMM uses the same pondering cat.

virality.summary: Know Your Meme traces the meme to Douglas Sacha's 2019 photo. The earliest memetic use is a TikTok by @rexiilol on 14 Jan 2025 ('Thinking what job imma get on the 19th of January'). By February 2025 captioned 'pondering cat' posts were everywhere on TikTok and Instagram Reels, alongside the look-alike 'Thinking Baby' meme. On Robinhood Chain the cat became $HMM, 'the sound your brain makes before you do something dumb', with a meme depot of 187 'certified hmm's' and buy-by-tweet via Wire bot. Tangem ranked it #8 among Robinhood Chain memes on 3 Sep 2026.
virality.metrics: @rexiilol TikTok (14 Jan 2025): 366,000+ plays and 93,000 likes in a month. @ofcoursecats Instagram (11 Feb 2025): 70,000+ likes and 40,000 reposts in two days. Know Your Meme entry: 26,675 views (all KYM). Coin: X @thinkingcatRH 3,041 followers (joined 19 Jul 2026); GeckoTerminal 15,810 holders; CoinGecko 1,087 watchlist users. A 3 Sep 2026 post about HMM by trader @CryptoKaleo drew 35,835 views. All read 2026-09-25 ~20:45 UTC.

cats.lore: Every trader knows the sound: hmm. In 2019 photographer Douglas Sacha shared a portrait of a tabby with a snowy chin, one white paw tucked under it, gazing into the distance as if weighing the universe. In January 2025 TikTok turned the photo into the Thinking Cat, the face of every overthought decision. When Robinhood Chain opened in 2026 the pondering cat moved in on Pons. It began as a developer's test token and was adopted by its community, who keep a depot of 187 'certified hmm's' and an 'ask the cat' button for anyone still deciding.

cats.name: Bundle Cat
cats.whoIsTheCat: Not a real cat. Bundle Cat is an original mascot: a fluffy ginger kitten in silver plate armour, with a pink bow and a longsword. It was made for Mosh, the Robinhood Chain launch tool built by UV Labs, and on 2 Sep 2026 it became Mosh's first launch, on the Pons launchpad. The @BundleCatAI account opened the same day.

virality.summary: A launch-venue mascot rather than an internet meme. In its first week Bundle Cat topped the Pons home page. UV Labs' Justin Bebis published an X article, 'Bundle Cat's Launch & How Mosh Actually Works' (9 Sep 2026): the 8 ETH raise was filled, about 72% of supply was locked in agent vaults, and AI agents trade it within fixed limits. The same day Bankless named BUN among five 'Robinhood Chain Hidden Gems'.

cats.lore: Bundle Cat is the smallest knight on Robinhood Chain: a fluffy ginger kitten in silver plate armour, a pink bow between the ears and a sword taller than itself. It was made as the mascot of Mosh, a launch tool from UV Labs, and on 2 September 2026 it became Mosh's very first launch on Pons. Its quest is to guard the bundle. The coins its backers pooled at launch stay locked in vaults for good, looked after by AI agents that follow strict rules. For its first week the kitten knight kept watch from the Pons home page.
